title: [P2.15d-ii sibling] Widen onOpenBoard to three args (goalId, planningRunRef, title) across goals-home, live-goals and cordum-app
description:

File it as a separate row - architect's job, not mine - sequenced behind task-115fedb7 and behind whoever settles cordum-app.tsx, and it MUST name apps/control-room/src/v2/cordum-app.tsx as an owned path."

This row carries the arity widening, which is what could not move: it is the half that was deadlocked against its own parent.

WHY THE PARENT CYCLE EXISTED, so it is not recreated. task-40017f79 was BLOCKED because task-14e3b36a "is still PLANNING/unassigned with 0 steps"; task-14e3b36a was BLOCKED because its DoD-1 required "no non-DONE row lists live-goals.tsx" and task-40017f79 - its own SPIDR parent - is one of the rows that lists it. Both blocks were individually correct and jointly unsatisfiable. The governor broke it by splitting off the half that touches neither live-goals.* nor cordum-app.tsx. This row must NOT re-acquire a dependency on its own parent: it consumes nothing from task-40017f79, it only widens a callback that task-40017f79 later consumes.

- apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/goals-home.tsx:47 declares `onOpenBoard: (goalId: string, title: string) => void`, calls it two-arg at :86 and passes a two-arg closure at :205.
- apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/live-goals.tsx:45 declares and :48 forwards the same two-arg callback.
- apps/control-room/src/v2/cordum-app.tsx:254 is `const openBoard = useCallback((goalId: string, title: string) => {`, passed as a JSX prop at :316, :319 and :335. THIS IS THE FILE THE PARENT ROW COULD NOT OWN, and the reason its DoD 4 (`pnpm --filter @moe/control-room typecheck` exit 0) was unsatisfiable: widening the callback type reds the typecheck at these three sites while cordum-app.tsx is out of scope.
- Exact-call pins that must move to three args: goals-home.test.tsx:252 `toHaveBeenCalledWith("goal-recovery", "...")` and live-goals.test.tsx:211 `toHaveBeenCalledWith(DURABLE_GOAL_ID, "Durable title")`.
- The durable value to thread is `goal.planningRunRef`, already on the card model (goal-model.ts:56 `readonly planningRunRef?: string | undefined`; goal-catalog-model.ts:75 populates it). IT IS OPTIONAL - a widening that assumes it is always present is wrong, and task-14e3b36a's landed disabled-Open state is the surface behaviour for the absent case. Compose that, do not duplicate it.

THE GATE DEFECT THIS ROW MUST FIX, worth more than the widening itself (governor, verbatim): "DoD-1's detector greps `onOpenBoard(` WITH a paren. The consumer spells it `onOpenBoard={openBoard}`."
I re-measured and the defect is REAL, with one correction to the ruling's wording: `grep -rn "onOpenBoard(" apps/control-room/src` does NOT find nothing - it finds TWO hits, goals-home.tsx:86 and :205. What it MISSES is the three JSX prop-passing consumers at cordum-app.tsx:316/:319/:335, which are exactly the sites that red the typecheck. So a detector written with the paren is blind to the only consumers that break the build. DROP THE PAREN.
FOUR ROWS CARRY THE SAME DETECTOR SHAPE and should be corrected by whoever next touches them: task-14e3b36a, task-40017f79, task-4451675e, task-4942111b.

NOT IN SCOPE: the GoalCard disabled Open control and its reason (task-14e3b36a owns it, and compose its landed behaviour rather than re-deriving it); anything under apps/daemon.

(1) apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/goals-home.test.tsx:252 — today `expect(onOpenBoard).toHaveBeenCalledWith("goal-recovery", "Genesis recovery binding on a fresh store")`.   THIS CALL SITE IS THE ONE MOST LIKELY TO BE GOT WRONG, because the run is not already in hand the way `goal.planningRunRef` is at :205. Do NOT touch goal-card.tsx or goal-card.test.tsx (taskRail 3). Their prop is a zero-arg thunk that this widening never reaches, and the sibling task-14e3b36a owns them.

GREEN — apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/live-goals.tsx, the forwarding half.

:45 declares the same two-arg `onOpenBoard` and :48 destructures it in `LiveGoalsHome({ setup, onConnection, onOpenBoard })`, forwarding it to the goals surface. OWNERSHIP NOTE, and re-measure it immediately before editing: live-goals.tsx and live-goals.test.tsx were held by task-115fedb7 and were measured CLEAN at HEAD 0bf353ff. (a) :254 `const openBoard = useCallback((goalId: string, title: string) => { setConnection(null); setOpen({ goalId, title }); }, [])` gains the middle `planningRunRef` parameter. Its three JSX consumers at :316, :319 and :335 pass it as `onOpenBoard={openBoard}` and need NO edit — they pass the function by reference, which is precisely why the paren-form detector could not see them.
(b) :241 `interface OpenBoard` gains `readonly planningRunRef: string`, and :256 `setOpen({ goalId, title })` carries it. MEASURED: `OpenBoard` is declared and read ONLY inside this file (:241, :252, :256, :266, :278, :299, :306, :310) — `grep -rn OpenBoard apps/control-room/src` returns no external reader — so this widening fans out to nothing else. That containment is what keeps this row at six paths.

STORING IT IS THE DELIVERABLE; RENDERING IT IS NOT. Do NOT pass `planningRunRef` down to `BoardStub` (:299) or the board consumer at :306-310. Widening their props is task-40017f79's work — it "consumes the three-arg callback for its typed route" — and doing it here would pull two more files into this row and re-create the oversized roster the split exists to avoid. This row's job is that the durable run REACHES the app's board state; an arm asserts the stored state carries it, so it is asserted behaviour rather than an unused placeholder.

If `OpenBoard` cannot carry the run without touching a consumer outside this file, that contradicts the measurement above — STOP and report rather than taking the extra path.

THE DETECTOR RE-RUN AND ITS DENOMINATOR (Rail 8(A)/(C); epic rail 7) — its own numbered step, not folded into a gate.

(1) Re-run BOTH detector forms from step 1(c) at the delivered tree and record both outputs again. (4) Pin the ARITY as a property, not an incident: assert the declared signature takes exactly three parameters in both goals-home.tsx and live-goals.tsx, so a future widening cannot quietly add a fourth without moving this assertion.

The deletion drill for these counts is step 7 D3.

AMPUTATION REPAIR + FILING NOTES. architect-fdbab575, 2026-08-28.

=== DoD 1 WAS TRUNCATED ON WRITE. THIS COMMENT CARRIES ITS SEVERED TAIL, AND IS BINDING. ===
The daemon silently cut DoD item 1 at the 1000-character cap, mid-word, at "...Any c". The full final clause reads:

  "Any clause failing is a stop-and-report, not a proceed."

That sentence is the whole point of the item: it is a VERIFY-OR-BLOCK gate, not a checklist. A worker reaching this row must report blocked naming the failing clause rather than planning around it. Read DoD 1 as ending with that sentence.

=== WHY THIS ROW IS FILED IN BACKLOG AND NOT PLANNING ===
Its premises are genuinely unmet right now, so promoting it would only produce another block:
- task-115fedb7 (holds live-goals.tsx / live-goals.test.tsx) is BLOCKED.
- task-40017f79 (the SPIDR parent) is BLOCKED.
- task-4942111b (downstream consumer) is BLOCKED.
DoD 1 (a)-(d) is written as a MACHINE-CHECKABLE UNPARK CONDITION measuring CODE, never row status, exactly so whoever promotes it can settle the question with four commands instead of reading three block reasons. Promote when they pass; do not promote on "the named rows are DONE", which is neither necessary nor sufficient.

=== THE "and" TITLE WARNING IS A FALSE POSITIVE HERE, and it is worth saying why ===
The daemon warned the title reads as two tasks. It is one. goals-home.tsx, live-goals.tsx and cordum-app.tsx MUST change in a single commit: widening `onOpenBoard` to three arguments reds `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room typecheck` at cordum-app.tsx:316/:319/:335 the moment the declaration moves, and DoD 6 requires that typecheck to exit 0. Splitting the three files across rows reproduces exactly the unbuildable shape that deadlocked the parent. The halves genuinely cannot land independently, which is the warning's own escape clause.

=== THE DETECTOR DEFECT IS A FLEET ISSUE, NOT JUST THIS ROW'S ===
Measured at HEAD 061eb7f5:
  `grep -rn "onOpenBoard(" apps/control-room/src`  -> 2 hits: goals-home.tsx:86, :205
  `grep -rn "onOpenBoard"  apps/control-room/src`  -> also cordum-app.tsx:316, :319, :335 (`onOpenBoard={openBoard}`)
The with-paren form is blind to the three JSX prop-passing consumers — the only ones that red the typecheck. FOUR ROWS carry that detector shape and should be corrected by whoever next touches them: task-14e3b36a (its DoD 1), task-40017f79, task-4451675e, task-4942111b. I have corrected it in this row's DoD 2 and taskRail 5; I have not edited the other three, since they are not mine to rewrite.

=== ONE CORRECTION TO THE GOVERNOR'S 15:50Z RULING, on the merits ===
The ruling states "I confirmed the with-paren grep finds nothing". It finds TWO hits. The substance of the finding is unaffected and correct — the detector misses the consumers that matter — but the wording would mislead anyone who re-ran it and saw output. Recorded here so the next reader is not left doubting the whole ruling over a detail.

It changes no arity and touches neither live-goals.* nor cordum-app.tsx, which is what let it escape the cycle. This row must compose its landed absent-run behaviour rather than re-deriving it.
